facts: The Project Gutenberg eBook of "The Great Gatsby" was released on January 17, 2021.
The eBook was last updated on January 26, 2025.
The eBook includes a table of contents with nine chapters.
The eBook features a dedication to Zelda.
The narrator's family is prominent in a Midwestern city.
The narrator moved to the East after World War I to pursue a career in the bond business.
Daisy wishes her daughter to be a "beautiful little fool."
Nick observes Gatsby reaching toward a distant green light.
The area known as the "valley of ashes" is characterized by ash-covered landscapes and the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg.
Tom Buchanan introduces the protagonist to his mistress, Myrtle Wilson, during a train journey to New York.
Myrtle Wilson's husband, George Wilson, owns the garage where they stop.
Tom strikes Myrtle during a confrontation when she mentions his wife, Daisy.
Jay Gatsby hosts extravagant summer parties at his mansion.
The narrator receives a formal invitation to one of Gatsby's parties.
A chaotic car accident occurs during one of the parties.
The narrator works at the Probity Trust during the summer.
Gatsby's mansion hosts guests who speculate about his mysterious past, including rumors of bootlegging and murder.
Gatsby introduces the narrator to Meyer Wolfshiem, a gambler linked to the 1919 World Series scandal.
Daisy Fay marries Tom Buchanan, despite Gatsby's past courtship of her.
Gatsby plans to invite Daisy to tea at Nick's house after hearing her name for the first time in years.
The narrator initially mistakes Gatsby's mansion for a party due to its bright lights.
Gatsby expresses a desire to invite Daisy over for tea.
Daisy is overwhelmed by Gatsby's collection of beautiful shirts, which brings her to tears.
The chapter concludes with the narrator feeling like an outsider as Gatsby and Daisy become absorbed in each other.
Gatsby was originally named James Gatz.
Gatsby worked for millionaire Dan Cody for five years.
Tom Buchanan suspects Gatsby of being a bootlegger.
Gatsby realizes he cannot repeat the past.
Gatsby dismisses his servants, prompting speculation about his health.
Tom Buchanan confronts Gatsby about his past at the Plaza Hotel.
Daisy admits she never loved Tom during the heated argument.
Myrtle dies in a hit-and-run accident involving Gatsby's car, which Daisy was driving.
The narrator struggles to sleep due to a foghorn and unsettling dreams.
Gatsby becomes dejected after waiting for Daisy, who ultimately did not come to him.
George Wilson becomes obsessed with finding the owner of the yellow car that killed Myrtle.
Gatsby's longing for Daisy intensifies, leading him to revisit Louisville.
Gatsby's father, Henry C. Gatz, arrives from Minnesota after Gatsby's death.
Nick Carraway struggles with isolation while trying to reach out to Daisy and Gatsby's acquaintances.
Gatsby's funeral is attended only by Gatz, Nick, and a few others.
Tom Buchanan and Daisy retreat into their privilege after causing destruction.
